learningObjective: Reason about MLIR Pass and PassManager semantics: op-scoping and pipeline nesting.

canonicalClaims.claim: MLIR passes declare the Op type they run on; a PassManager iterates a pass over every matching Op. Nested pass managers compose pipelines at different scopes (typically ModuleOp containing FuncOp-scoped passes).
nonImplications: Does not imply nested pass managers must exist; simple single-scope pipelines are allowed.
Does not imply the scope choice is arbitrary; passes rely on being called at the right level.

misconceptions.claim: All MLIR passes are module-level and must walk functions manually.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Function-scoped passes (`func.func` scope) are first-class; PassManager iterates over each function automatically.

misconceptions.claim: MLIR runs passes in parallel by default.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Default execution is sequential in declared order; per-op parallelism at a nested scope is opt-in.
The framework verifies scope; a pass built for FuncOp cannot be attached to a Module-level PM without nesting.

misconceptions.claim: A pass may freely modify any op in the IR regardless of scope.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Passes with `IsIsolatedFromAbove` scope may not modify ops outside their region without explicit design.
